clue.text: US convicts collapsing, is dry bread not providing energy?

indicators.note: something collapsing falls into disorder, so the letters fall out of their order
not providing something means leaving it out, so the physics symbol for energy is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy, and it is removed

explanation.surface: Prisoners are fed stale, dry bread that gives them no energy, and they start collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E out of IS DRY BREAD and rearrange the rest to get YARDBIRDS, also the name of the band Jimmy Page played in before Led Zeppelin.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardbird is American slang for a prison inmate, from the exercise yard, so the plural means convicts.

clue.text: Almost agreed for Sloane Ranger to tour key Black Sea resort

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
to tour a place is to go round it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a posh Sloane Ranger says 'yah' for yes; almost all of it leaves the first two letters
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A posh young Londoner agrees to go on a tour of a fashionable Black Sea resort.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a stereotypical upper-class young Londoner from around Sloane Square, whose way of saying yes is 'yah'. Key looks like a musical key or an island; it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a seaside town in Crimea on the Black Sea coast, famous as the site of the 1945 conference.

clue.text: No lead 15? Strange record for Priest, maybe

definitions.note: a ritualist is a person; the clue offers a priest as one example

indicators.note: with no lead, the word loses the letter at its front
strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: the answer to 15 across, minus its first letter
to list is to record, and a list is a record

explanation.surface: A record by Judas Priest sounds strange because it has no lead guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across is GUITAR; drop its first letter and rearrange UITAR. Judas Priest is a heavy metal band, which helps the surface's music theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritualist is someone devoted to religious rites, and a priest who performs them strictly is a typical example.

clue.text: Appearing sleepless, British LSD advocate Observer finally featured

parts.note: standard abbreviation for British
Timothy Leary, the American psychologist who championed LSD
the eye is what observes

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the following word, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the last letter of featured

explanation.surface: A British newspaper column on an LSD enthusiast, appearing in the Observer, shows him looking sleepless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, which makes it look like a publication rather than an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bleary-eyed has dim, unfocused eyes, the look of a person who has not slept.

clue.text: Masses heard in French cathedral city

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the word sounds when spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: reams are masses, as in reams of paper

explanation.surface: Masses can be heard sung in a French cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Masses suggests church services, which fits the cathedral; it is really just a large quantity. The English pronunciation of the city is the same as reams.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheims (Reims) in north-east France has the Gothic cathedral where French kings were crowned.

clue.text: Dropped painter outside front of gallery after lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word turns it upside down so it reads from bottom to top
outside means one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: first letter of gallery

explanation.surface: A painter's picture was dropped outside the front of the gallery after being lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGAS read upwards gives SAGED, which then wraps around G.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagged means sank or drooped downwards, as dropped can mean.

clue.text: Leaves summons

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sheets of a book
second meaning: calls someone over a loudspeaker or pager

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs (goes away, calls); only the second is a verb, the first is the noun for sheets of paper. Jimmy Page of Led Zeppelin lurks in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaves of a book are its sheets, and to call for someone by public address system is to page them.

clue.text: For PM under pressure, computer work takes time

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
information technology
T is the symbol for time

explanation.surface: A prime minister under pressure finds that computer work takes up time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' and 'takes' just set the pieces in order: P, then IT, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt the Elder and William Pitt the Younger were both British Prime Ministers.

clue.text: Old composer upset scruffy heavy metal fan

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: standard abbreviation for old
Alban Berg, the Austrian composer

explanation.surface: An old classical composer is upset by a scruffy fan of heavy metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebo is British slang for a long-haired, unkempt follower of heavy rock or metal music.

clue.text: Learned secret about husband wearing coral pants

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within the other
about means around, so one word goes round the rest

parts.note: sly means secretive or underhand

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are treated as a mess and rearranged

parts.note: standard abbreviation for husband
taken as written; the husband wears it, so goes in with it

explanation.surface: A husband secretly wears coral-coloured trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like the trousers the husband is wearing, but here it is the slang judgement 'rubbish' that signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned, said as two syllables, describes someone with deep scholarly knowledge, a close synonym.

clue.text: What Wogan jocularly recalled as "river from hell"

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the backward direction

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?
Tel was the jokey nickname for Terry Wogan

explanation.surface: Terry Wogan joked about remembering some river as hellish.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Wogan was an Irish broadcaster on BBC radio and TV; Tel is the matey short form of Terry. Recalled seems to mean remembered, which suits a river of forgetting.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Lethe is one of the rivers of Hades, the underworld; drinking from it made the dead forget.

clue.text: Violet Elizabeth reading out last three pieces from Keats for anniversary?

definitions.note: the question mark flags an example: an eightieth is one particular anniversary

indicators.note: the last three pieces of the following name are its closing three letters

parts.note: the closing three letters of the poet's name

indicators.note: reading out means saying letters aloud, in the lisping voice of this character

parts.note: A, T, S spoken as letters with a lisp turning the S sound into TH

explanation.surface: A lisping girl reads out a few lines of Keats at an anniversary event.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott, in Richmal Crompton's Just William books, lisps ('I'll thcream and thcream'). Said as letters, A-T-S sounds like 'eighties'; her lisp makes it 'eightieth'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightieth is the anniversary marking eighty years, such as an eightieth birthday.

clue.text: Treated thus, get partner Peter Grant

parts.note: surface reading: someone trying to get a partner for a man called Peter Grant
setter's reading: the letters of 'get partner' rearranged spell Peter Grant, so the clue names the process applied to them

explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the phrase 'get partner' has had its letters reordered to give Peter Grant, Led Zeppelin's famous manager, and the answer describes what was done.
explanation.definitionFit: A word that has been anagrammed has had its letters rearranged into a new word or phrase, exactly the treatment shown.

clue.text: Pitch error Lulu occasionally makes

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The singer Lulu sometimes sings off pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like musical tuning; it is the ship's motion. Lulu is a Scottish pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch and roll are both ways a ship or aircraft rocks, and pitch can also mean to lurch or roll about.

clue.text: Script due a daft comic device

indicators.note: daft means silly, so the letters are jumbled foolishly

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedy script is due to include a daft gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A custard pie thrown in someone's face is a classic slapstick gag, so a comic device.

clue.text: Stay in central Crimea in the same place

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
central means the middle, so only the letters at the heart of the word are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of the six
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: A traveller stays in central Crimea, never moving from the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: Stay looks like the definition of a verb meaning remain; it is the wordplay, and the definition is the bibliographic phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is the Latin footnote term, shortened to ibid., meaning the source cited is the same as before.

clue.text: Plant and Page song shows teamwork

parts.note: to plant a body is to inter or bury it
P is the abbreviation for page
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Robert Plant and Jimmy Page on a song show how well they work together.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant and Page are Led Zeppelin's singer and guitarist, but here they are a verb (bury) and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Interplay is the way parts or people act on one another, close to cooperative teamwork.

clue.text: Deserter, one retreating behind curt Guy Gibson, perhaps

indicators.note: curt means cut short, so the next word loses its final letter

parts.note: Guy shortened

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts their side
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A deserter retreats behind the brusque wartime hero Guy Gibson.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Gibson led the Dambusters raid, but Gibson here is the guitar make, and Guy is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibson is an American make of electric guitar, famously the Les Paul played by Jimmy Page.

clue.text: Function film star Richard hosts at home, serving fruit

parts.note: tan is short for tangent, a trigonometric function

indicators.note: someone who hosts has guests inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Richard Gere, the Hollywood actor
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A film star hosts a function at his home and serves fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Function suggests a party, but it is the maths function. GERE holds IN. Tangerine is also a Led Zeppelin song.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Called singer that fronts Zeppelin

parts.note: a tit is a songbird
the first word of the band's name, Led Zeppelin

explanation.surface: The singer who fronts Led Zeppelin is being named.
explanation.walkthrough: The singer who fronts Zeppelin is Robert Plant, but singer here is a bird. LED is the word that fronts Zeppelin in the band's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Titled means given a name or title, so a book titled X is called X.

clue.text: Tight bassist at the end of Synchronicity

parts.note: Sting, bassist and singer of the Police

indicators.note: the end of a word is its closing letter alone

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: The Police's bassist plays tight at the end of their album Synchronicity.
explanation.walkthrough: Synchronicity was the Police's last studio album, which suits Sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal for mean with money, which is what stingy means.

clue.text: Electronic snag besets sophisticated scientific equipment

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem
E as the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: An electronic fault plagues some sophisticated scientific kit.
explanation.walkthrough: HITCH goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech means advanced technology, here used as a noun for such advanced equipment.

clue.text: Trendy A-lister finding stage for Scorpions

parts.note: in means fashionable
an A-list celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A trendy celebrity gets a stage spot for the rock band Scorpions.
explanation.walkthrough: Scorpions is a German hard rock band, so stage looks like a concert platform; it is a growth stage of the arachnid.
explanation.definitionFit: An instar is a phase between moults in arthropods such as insects and scorpions.

clue.text: Retro funk's back — my kind of music

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so everything after it reads in reverse
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of funk
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: A fan of retro funk declares it the best kind of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My kind of music' looks like a phrase; 'my' is the exclamation COR. Funk looks like the music genre too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is a genre of popular music, the one Led Zeppelin played.

clue.text: A little decoy puzzled rodent

indicators.note: a little of the words means just a part of them, a run of letters inside

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A small decoy left the rodent confused.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: The German roar going around pub is a sign food's ready

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: der is a German word for the
an inn is a pub
to bell is to bellow, as a stag does

explanation.surface: A German's roar goes around the pub, signalling food is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Roar suggests noise from the German; it is the verb bell, the bellow of a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner bell is rung to tell people that a meal is served.

clue.text: Heartless Beatle describing McCartney's first as dud

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece goes around the other
heartless means with the middle cut out, so central letters go
first of the following word keeps only its opening letter, dropping the rest

parts.note: John Lennon; its middle NN removed
the first letter of McCartney

explanation.surface: A heartless Beatle described McCartney's first solo effort as a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the heart of LENNON leaves LEON, which goes around M.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is informal for something useless that fails to work, just as a dud is.

clue.text: Perhaps Stairway to Heaven second last for Apollo Zeppelin gig

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: last for the following words means taking the closing letter from each

parts.note: the final letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Stairway to Heaven was perhaps the second-to-last number at a Led Zeppelin gig at the Apollo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second last' reads as one phrase meaning penultimate, but it splits: S, then last letters. The Apollo is a London concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stairway to Heaven is Led Zeppelin's best-known song, so an example of one.

clue.text: Bury explosive Tory tales

indicators.note: something explosive blows apart, so the letters scatter and land differently

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants to bury some explosive stories about the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay to rest is a euphemism for burying the dead, or for putting an issue aside for good.

clue.text: Prince on an hour after midnight? Legend! He ruled

parts.note: Pr. is an abbreviation for prince
one o'clock in the morning, 1 AM, with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A legendary prince parties till an hour after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition calls on legend: he is a ruler from myth, not history.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the legendary king of Troy during the Trojan War, so a ruler from legend.

clue.text: Babyish solver no good

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you
standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A setter teases the solver as childish and useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Babyish means like an infant, and young means of few years; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Stewed hare bones and vegetable

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked down and mixed up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook's stew of hare bones served with vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse bean is the broad bean, a large-seeded variety grown as a vegetable and for fodder.
